intro: One of four labour codes in force since 21 November 2025. Replaces the Industrial Disputes Act, Trade Unions Act and Standing Orders Act — covering hiring and firing rules, strikes, unions and dispute resolution.

sections.p: Employers can hire workers on fixed-term contracts, who must get the same wages, hours and benefits as permanent workers doing the same work, and pro-rata gratuity.
Establishments with 300 or more workers must have standing orders setting out conditions of service, misconduct and disciplinary procedures.
Factories, mines and plantations with 300 or more workers need government permission before laying off, retrenching or closing (the earlier limit was 100). States may raise this limit.
Retrenched workers get 15 days' average pay for every completed year of service, plus 15 days' wages paid by the employer into a reskilling fund.
Workers in any establishment must give 14 days' notice before a strike, and can't strike during conciliation or tribunal proceedings. Earlier, notice was required only in public utility services.
Each establishment with 20 or more workers needs a Grievance Redressal Committee. Workers can approach the Industrial Tribunal directly if conciliation fails within the set time.
